content.text:
Names on a sheet are now unique: two names count as the same if they differ only in letter case or in spaces before or after them. `bin/e2e` passes.

- **Names are trimmed:** `ValidatePerson` removes spaces before and after a name, so it is saved and shown that way (" Cam " is stored as "Cam").
- **Duplicates are refused:** before adding or saving, `People` checks whether anyone else on the sheet already has the name, ignoring case. When editing, the person being edited is left out of that check, so they can keep their own name. A duplicate raises the new `DuplicatePersonNameException`, which its handler returns as a 409 error, and nothing is saved.
- **The database blocks duplicates too:** a new migration, `V3__person_name_unique.sql`, trims names already stored, adds a lowercase copy of the name (`name_key`) and a unique index on sheet plus that copy. This stops duplicates if two users add the same name at the same moment; that collision is caught and shown as the same error.
- **The form shows the error:** a refused add or edit shows the existing `person-form-error`. I reworded its text to cover the new rule: "A person needs a name not already on the sheet and a grade of A, B or C."

If a sheet already held two names that differ only by case or surrounding spaces, the new unique index would make the migration fail. That can't happen in this app's current setup, because its in-memory database starts empty on every run, but it would matter if the database ever kept data between runs.
